passage.quote: A short bullet summary gives a faithful abbreviated account of the same responsibility. The full text remains the complete description. The agent creates a summary when creating a description and maintains it whenever the description or its metadata changes. Summaries belong to the project’s versioned account and preserve the conditions and limitations needed to understand the behavior being promised. Older content and drafts without summaries remain readable.

from.quote: The summary is an optional summary array in the description’s JSON metadata, with one nonempty text string per bullet. An omitted or empty array means no summary. Loading and CLI inspection return it with the description, including at historical revisions. Validation rejects malformed bullets while keeping the full Markdown readable as a draft. Summary edits use the same file snapshots and affected-description review as other metadata edits.

The summary is an optional summary array in the description’s JSON metadata, with one nonempty text string per bullet. An omitted or empty array means no summary. Loading and CLI inspection return it with the description, including at historical revisions. Validation rejects malformed bullets while keeping the full Markdown readable as a draft. The full description supplies the complete account. Its summary preserves the qualifications that matter to understanding its promises, while leaving detailed explanations to the full text. A summary must not introduce a different promise or conceal an important limitation. Whenever the coding agent creates or changes a description or its metadata, it creates a missing summary and reviews existing bullets for accuracy. Changed promises, conditions, and limitations are reflected in both; accurate bullets need not be rewritten.

passage.quote: Whenever creating or changing a description or its metadata, create a nonempty `summary` array if missing and review any existing summary against the full description. Update the bullets in the same change when promises, conditions, or limitations change; retain accurate bullets when they still apply. Use concise, self-contained strings that summarize the responsibility’s behavior, not a list of topics, children, or code files. Keep implementation passage links in the full description. The file format permits absent summaries for older content and drafts, but that compatibility is not a reason to omit a summary from newly created or changed descriptions.

summary: Bullet summaries condense a responsibility’s behavior, conditions, and boundaries while the full description remains the complete account.
Agents create missing summaries whenever descriptions are created or changed and update existing bullets when their meaning changes. Older content and drafts remain readable without them.
Summaries share the description’s metadata, identity, and Git history. The desktop displays them; implementation links stay in the full text.
